FDA's rare disease framework faces its first real test in Capricor’s DMD drug
snippet: Last month, the FDA committed to designing a "fit-for-purpose" framework for regulating rare disease therapies based on patient need and realistically attainable evidence. With the upcoming decision for Capricor’s Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy deramiocel, this paradigm faces its first key test.

title: Coherus cuts 30% of staffers, Gyre makes post-acquisition layoffs
snippet: Coherus is narrowing its pipeline projects while Gyre reorganizes after an acquisition, with both biotechs conducting workforce reductions.

title: BIO pitches US plan to beat China in biotech ‘space race’
snippet: The seven proposals in the Bio Advance plan include easing clinical trial starts, boosting manufacturing and establishing a new White House office to coordinate the government’s biotech policy.

title: Beam preps FDA run for industry-first base-edited therapy after pivotal sickle cell success
snippet: Beam Therapeutics' risto-cel provided at least 12 consecutive months of freedom from severe pain crises for patients with sickle cell disease in a mid-stage trial, setting the stage for an FDA application as early as this year.

title: Bayer wins first-in-class FDA nod for blood thinner, setting stage for BMS-J&J rival
snippet: Bayer’s Sunharbo has secured the first FDA approval of its class, establishing a regulatory pathway for other factor XIa inhibitors, such as Bristol Myers Squibb and Johnson and Johnson’s milvexian.

title: Delix raises $100M to advance at-home psychedelic without hallucinogenic effects
snippet: The series C raise, co-led by Johnson & Johnson’s venture capital arm, will help Delix Therapeutics push its novel psychedelic asset into mid-stage development for major depressive disorder.

title: Altimmune gears up for FDA meeting on pivotal Phase 3 trial in alcohol use disorder
snippet: Having linked its glucagon/GLP-1 candidate to a significant reduction in heavy drinking days, Altimmune is preparing to speak to the FDA in December about the design of a Phase 3 program.

title: BioSpace 2027 Best Places to Work shines light on most admired employers
snippet: The list honors 50 life sciences employers of choice. Employees at SERB Pharmaceuticals and CSL Behring share why their companies stand out.

title: FDA orders class-wide GLP-1 label update to include potential risk for rare eye disease
snippet: Twelve marketed drugs, including Eli Lilly’s and Novo’s weight loss mega-blockbusters, will require a label change under the new FDA update.

title: Boehringer, Zealand’s obesity drug doesn’t elevate heart risk in key late-stage test
snippet: The Phase 3 results help clarify the safety profile of Zealand and Boehringer Ingelheim’s survodutide, but analysts do not think the drug will find utility beyond patients with liver-related risk factors.

title: Lilly to seek second sleep apnea approval after Foundayo reduces disease severity in Phase 3
snippet: If approved, the oral GLP-1 would be Eli Lilly’s second marketed drug for obstructive sleep apnea after the GIP/GLP-1 injectable Zepbound secured the first approval in the space in December 2024.

title: Vir's hepatitis delta combo tamps down virus as Gilead showdown looms
snippet: Vir Biotechnology is targeting a mid-2027 regulatory submission for its monthly chronic hepatitis delta regimen, with head-to-head data against Gilead’s Hepcludex expected next quarter.

title: Update: Compass submits psilocybin depression drug for approval after stock wobbles
snippet: Compass Pathways has completed an FDA filing for COMP360, with an expected launch in the first half of next year. The update follows a reported regulatory submission for Usona Institute’s own psilocybin candidate for depression last Monday.

title: J&J and Protagonist’s Icotyde improves psoriatic arthritis but AbbVie’s Skyrizi likely to reign
snippet: A Phase 3 trial showed that Johnson & Johnson and Protagonist Therapeutics’ oral therapy Icotyde improved psoriatic arthritis symptoms but AbbVie’s injectable is likely to hold court based on higher efficacy, analysts say.

title: Details from Novartis’ failed cardiovascular trial offer ‘little silver lining’ for rivals
snippet: Full data from the Phase 3 HORIZON trial of Novartis' pelacarsen failed to show any apparent benefit, leading analysts to further reduce the odds of success for Lp(a)-lowering competitors such as Amgen’s olpasiran.

title: Argenx buyout of peptide engine and Big Pharma favorite UNP could top $1B
snippet: Unnatural Products has risen from founder Joshua Schwochert’s garage to an acquisition deal, valued at up to $1.15 billion, to join argenx.

title: Update: FDA investigates Novartis' Zolgensma following 9 cases of tumors in treated patients
snippet: After Novartis confirmed the reports of tumors in patients who have been treated with the spinal muscular atrophy gene therapy, the FDA will determine if any regulatory action is needed for Zolgensma or for the pharma's similar product Itvisma.

title: Shortly after Vertex acquisition, Crinetics will cut 78 employees
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: Novo’s troubled cardio drug could find niche in less sick patients
snippet: At the American Heart Association conference, investigators were supportive of further studying Novo’s IL-6 inhibitor ziltivekimab in patients with less severe cardiovascular and kidney disease.

title: With an approval apiece, the verdict is still out on AbbVie’s and BMS’ twin neuro buys
snippet: After emraclidine’s schizophrenia fail and Cobenfy’s laggard launch, it’s too early to know who made the better buy: AbbVie, in its $8.7 billion Cerevel takeover in late 2023, or Bristol Myers Squibb, which spent $14 billion for Karuna just two weeks later.

title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
